title: Normalized sectionwise abelian transpose of the scalar coefficient-unit comparison
statement: In the setting of lem-sp-tower-scalar-unit-abelian-transpose-section, with eY and eX fixed to the unique ordinary adjuncts of scalarGenerator, the values at every tower level, pro-etale chart and section of the two displayed abelian transpose morphisms are equal.

source.place: Paragraph (2): normalized ordinary coefficient-unit calculation before extension from constant integer sections.

proof.text: Expand the composite adjunction and use homEquiv naturality. The canonical scalar adjuncts become scalarGenerator; the two maps are now the forgotten scalar generator followed by the geometric coefficient adjunct, and the abelian adjunct of forgetIso followed by unitIso and scalarGenerator.

Precompose with integerGenerator. Naturality of the componentwise abelian adjunction and d.unit_normalization identify the right path with the adjunct of integerPull followed by the target integer and scalar generators. On each constant integer section, scalarGenerator is the coefficient ring map, the normalized geometric coefficient adjunct is the constant ring direct-image map, and both ring maps preserve integer casts. The identity-on-sections equation for chi identifies the left path with the same integer section. The constant-sheaf universal property extends this equality to integer towers.

source.place: Paragraph (2): normalized ordinary coefficient-unit calculation before extension from constant integer sections.

proof.text: Cancel integerGenerator: transport both candidate maps back through chi and lift them through the integral forgetful functor, using its proved fully-faithful construction in TowerRestrictedScalarAdjunction. Their values on one agree by the defining constant-integer equation. Mathlib SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv identifies maps out of the regular module with its target global sections, so the lifted maps agree. Forget again, cancel chi inverse, and evaluate the resulting equality at the requested level, chart and section.
